notes: Apple defines SPTM for A15-or-later SoCs, which includes the A17 Pro by ordering. No public A17 Pro SPTM research specific to 27.0.1 was located. 2026-11-12: manifest metadata shows an SPTM image for the target build (C-157, C-159). Apple states that the kernel cannot write page-table entries on SPTM-protected products without naming them (C-145). No A17 Pro runtime evidence.
The only SPTM bypass mention is a community reference describing an undisclosed bypass. No public technical disclosure was found.

Apple's iOS 27 and iOS 27.2 notes list kernel-memory write and corruption entries (research/apple-27x-cve-mapping.md). iOS 27: 2 write and 7 corruption entries, one of them Calif.io-credited (CVE-2026-28968). iOS 27.2: 4 write, 12 corruption and 1 copy-on-write entry. Applicability to iOS 27.0.1 is not established, because the advisories state no affected version range.

Apple lists kernel-memory read, disclosure and layout impacts: eight on the iOS 27 page (including CVE-2026-84622, which needs root) and six on the iOS 27.2 page. Applicability to iOS 27.0.1 is not established. No public technical analysis or exploit was reviewed.
Apple lists write and corruption impacts for kernel memory on the iOS 27 and iOS 27.2 pages. None is shown to affect iOS 27.0.1. No public write-up or reproduction was found (C-049).

Apple lists a WebContent sandbox escape reachable by a remote attacker (iOS 27.2: CVE-2026-112690) and a WebKit Process Model escape (iOS 27.2: CVE-2026-113897). It also lists a kernel entry where a sandboxed app may execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges (iOS 27: CVE-2026-84607). These are Apple-listed fixes. Applicability to iOS 27.0.1 is not established. No verified public sandbox escape for the target exists. External reports (A19 Pro configuration, 27.0.1) state boundary crossings into other containers, not transferred to the target (see CMP-016).

Apple lists a kernel entry in which a malicious app may gain root privileges (iOS 27: CVE-2026-43689) and an entry in which an app with root privileges reads uninitialised kernel memory (iOS 27: CVE-2026-84622). The iOS 27.2 page lists no kernel privilege entry. No verified public privilege escalation for the target was found.
AMFI (code signing enforcement) was not researched in this pass. Scheduled for the next research update.

A complete chain is reported only for an iPhone 18 Pro (A20 Pro) demonstration. Apple's notes list six Calif.io-credited entries in 27.2 and four in 27.0. None of the six 27.2 entries is a kernel-memory impact. One 27.0 entry (CVE-2026-28968) is a kernel corruption impact. Apple's notes do not identify the demonstration's chain. No write-up has been published (C-049).

No bootstrap for iOS 27.0.1 is verified. Dopamine's 3.0.2 to 3.0.13 release notes do not mention iOS 27 (C-055). The 3.0 release states that real-device SPTM support ends at iOS 17.3.1 (C-066). Its Titan bypass covers iOS 16.5.1 to 17.3.1 (C-065). A third-party table lists A14 to A17 for iOS 17.3.1 and earlier (C-016). The current Dopamine README lists no iOS 27 range (C-133). The Procursus README states no iOS range in the lines read (C-135). Not established for the target. 2026-11-12 re-check: default-branch heads and release records unchanged (C-167).

Sileo's latest release is 2.5.1 (2024-10-08), with no iOS 27 mention (C-030). The former ElleKit repository identifier redirects to tealbathingsuit/ellekit, which has no GitHub release (C-056). An upstream claim that ElleKit 1.2 covers iOS 27 is unverified (C-057). Package-manager readiness for iOS 27.0.1 is not established. The official ElleKit repository states no version range and has no release (C-134). The latest Sileo release is 2.5.1 (2024-10-08). Not established for the target. 2026-11-12 re-check: default-branch heads and release records unchanged (C-167).

Reboot persistence is reported for the iPhone 18 Pro demonstration (C-004). An over-the-air persistence demonstration on iOS 27.2 with Lockdown Mode is reported by the upstream reference (C-053). Neither is verified for the target.

No publicly installable tool is verified for this target (C-028). A public repository described as an A12/A13 PPL bypass exists (C-058). By its own description it does not apply to the target. A November 2026 project announcement claims iOS 27.0 to 27.0.1 support on the target model; no release was reviewed in this pass (C-064). None of these was reviewed or executed.

No independent reproduction on A17 Pro hardware was found. The announced kernel read/write work has no published write-up or code as of 2026-11-12 (C-049). A reported crash reproduction on another model exists (C-062). This project does not test exploit code on any real device.

Build 24A446 for iPhone16,2 is corroborated by third-party sources and by the Apple index date. An Apple-hosted BuildManifest (27.0.1, 24A446, iPhone16,2) was retrieved by range request on 2026-11-12, and its KernelCache digest matches the retrieved container (C-078). The complete package was not hashed, so verification remains partial.

The SKVLENT repository states boundary crossings into other applications' containers and shared groups on an A19 Pro configuration (27.0.1). These are repository statements. No A17 Pro evidence exists. Kernel read, kernel write and a jailbreak are stated as not demonstrated. Not transferred to the target. 2026-11-12: the README wording for direction 10 is a container-boundary crossing in userland, not kernel code execution (C-165).

The declared iOS range includes 27.0.1 by range only. The project names no device or SoC, and its repository records no device reports. It documents no kernel access, bootstrap, root or persistence. It warns of possible data loss. A17 Pro compatibility is not established. 2026-11-12: the README header and supported list disagree on the iOS 26 upper bound (26.7.2 against 26.6.2), and the 0.3.1 tweak note differs from the README FAQ (C-166).

Manifest-level differences only. The A17 Pro package lists no exclave-related component in any identity. The A18 Pro and A19 Pro packages list six per erase identity. The chip-token mapping is unresolved. The reason for the difference and any behavioural effect are not established. 2026-11-12: all three BuildIdentities of each inspected A17 Pro manifest were enumerated (C-157). The chip-identifier pairing is partially verified (C-160).

Secure Exclaves applicability to the target. Manifest metadata shows no exclave-named component in any of the three A17 Pro BuildIdentities for build 24A446 (and for the other two inspected builds). The target kernelcache and SPTM contain exclave-prefixed identifiers as static strings. Apple's article names no A17 Pro product. No device, runtime or independent evidence. Status: not established. The A18 Pro and A19 Pro rows of the reconciliation are manifest-level only and are not evidence for the target.

Chip identifier for the target. The manifest ApChipID 0x8130 and a community wiki identifier T8130 agree. The SPTM monitor token t8122 differs from the ApChipID and is not mapped to a marketing name by any authoritative source reviewed. The XNU repository groups T8122 with T8130 in one board configuration. Partially verified; the marketing mapping rests on a non-authoritative source.
